 Super Eagles star Umar Sadiq returns from injury to save Valencia
 Faruq Ibrahim
 23:38 - 01 November 2026
 Image
 Umar Sadiq enjoyed a heroic return, powering Valencia to victory against Elche.
 Advertisement
 Umar Sadiq marked his return from a two-month injury layoff with a decisive 69th-minute winner as Valencia ground out a gritty 1-0 away victory over Elche at the Estadio Manuel Martínez Valero on Sunday evening.
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 The encounter proved to be a frustrating affair for the hosts, who dominated possession and territory but lacked a cutting edge. 
 Relying on a pragmatic game plan, Javier Aguirre’s Valencia side absorbed pressure and executed a flawless second-half counter-attack to snatch all three points, handing the new manager his first victory since taking charge of the struggling club.
 Key match details
 Advertisement
 Advertisement
 Elche controlled the tempo from the opening whistle. However, breaking down the visitors' organised defensive block proved incredibly difficult. 
 MUST READ: Umar Sadiq's previous heroics 
 The hosts came closest to breaking the deadlock in the first half when Lucas Cepeda rattled the crossbar, but they ultimately failed to convert their territorial dominance into a tangible advantage.
 The complexion of the match shifted completely when Aguirre turned to his bench, introducing Umar Sadiq in the 60th minute for Pablo Maffeo.

 Making his first appearance since the end of August, the Super Eagles striker required less than ten minutes to alter the course of the game. In the 69th minute, a rapid Valencia transition sparked by goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski and Javi Guerra carved Elche open. 
 Arnaut Danjuma threaded a smart pass into the path of Sadiq, who expertly bypassed midfielder Gonzalo Villar before finishing clinically to give the visitors a 1-0 lead.
 Elche pressed desperately for an equaliser in the closing stages, forcing Dimitrievski into a series of vital interventions. The Valencia goalkeeper's standout moment arrived deep into stoppage time when he produced a phenomenal block to deny Federico Redondo, preserving the clean sheet and sealing the 1-0 win.
